versions.title: Version history
versions.purgeWarning: This makes the version unobtainable. Its file is deleted.
versions.purgeCaseLive: This version is what the resource is serving now, so the preview and the search index go with it — serving falls back to v{fallback} and both are rebuilt from that version’s content.
versions.purgeCaseLiveLast: This version is what the resource is serving now, and there is no version left to fall back to: the resource is left with no file, and nothing is rebuilt.
versions.purgeCaseNotLive: This version is not what the resource is serving. What is being served, its preview and its search index are unchanged.
versions.purgeCaseMayMove: That describes the resource as it is right now. Serving can move before you confirm — another run publishing, or a revert — in which case the deletion follows whatever is live then.
versions.purgeWarningTail: If you need this version’s content, download it first. Whichever case this is, rows may remain in versioning’s internal storage, where deletion is not guaranteed (history retained for other resources can reference the same files). Where storage versioning is enabled, the superseded object expires after its retention window (30 days by default). This cannot be undone.
versions.reasonPlaceholder: Reason for the deletion (recorded in the audit log)
versions.diffSchemaChanged: The columns changed, so a row-level diff is not available.
versions.purgeWarningSameContent: Other versions hold the same content ({versions}). Deleting this one does not erase it, and the resource may go back to serving that version’s copy. Delete them individually if they must go too.

diffUnavailable.purged: One of the versions has been deleted, so a diff is not available.
diffUnavailable.no-previous-version: This is the first version, so there is nothing to compare against.
diffUnavailable.not-ingested: v{version} has no row-level snapshot, so there is nothing to compare against. Where a reason was recorded, the version list shows it.
diffUnavailable.key-missing: A key column is not in v{version}, so its rows cannot be identified and no diff is available. Correcting the key applies from the next version on.
diffUnavailable.key-null: A key column of v{version} has empty values, so its rows cannot be identified and no diff is available. Correcting the key applies from the next version on.
diffUnavailable.key-not-unique: The key of v{version} does not identify a row, so no diff is available. Correcting the key applies from the next version on.

noTable.ragged-rows: rows do not split into the same columns

columnSettings.title: Primary key
columnSettings.help: The columns used to match a row to the same row in another version. With a key, a diff can count the rows that changed.
columnSettings.loadError: Could not load the column settings
columnSettings.noColumns: No columns have been interpreted yet. They become selectable once the pipeline has run.
columnSettings.willClear: Applying removes the primary key. From then on, editing one row shows in a diff as one row added and one removed.
columnSettings.willApply: Applying creates one version, and versions from there on are ingested under this key.
columnSettings.carried: The current version is ingested under this key.
columnSettings.pending: Set, but no version has been ingested under it yet.
columnSettings.queued: Applied. A rebuild is queued to create the version ingested under this key.
columnSettings.queueFailed: Applied, but the rebuild could not be queued — no version will be read under this key until one runs. Use “Queue the rebuild” to try again.

fault.key-missing: That column is not in the current content. As it stands, a version ingested under this key would be left out of diff ingestion.
fault.key-null: A column of this key has empty values. As it stands, a version ingested under this key would be left out of diff ingestion.
fault.key-not-unique: This key does not narrow a row down to one. As it stands, a version ingested under this key would be left out of diff ingestion.

unchecked.no-preview: The current content could not be read, so whether this key narrows a row down to one could not be checked. Applying still works.
unchecked.preview-stale: The interpretation has not caught up with the current content, so whether this key narrows a row down to one could not be checked. Applying still works.

noSample.no-preview: There is no interpretation to show a sample from yet.
noSample.preview-stale: A sample would be of the previous content, so none is shown — the interpretation has not caught up with what the resource is serving.

columnSettings.rebuildQueued: The rebuild is queued. It takes a few minutes; the sample appears the next time this is opened after it finishes.
columnSettings.confirmCost: Applying creates one version, but that version is left out of diff ingestion, so no diff involving it can be shown — not even rows added and removed. Correcting the key later does not bring it back in, because a past version’s diff is not changed after the fact. If the content that arrives next satisfies this key, versions from there on are ingested.
columnSettings.requirements: The columns you choose — the combination, if more than one — have to be present in the content, hold no empty values, and not repeat across rows. A column marked unique meets all three on its own. Where they are not met, the reason is shown before you apply.
columnSettings.noCounts: This version does not record per-column duplicate and empty counts, so nothing can be marked unique — it was interpreted before those were kept. Choose and check, or rebuild the interpretation.
columnSettings.stability: One more that cannot be checked in advance: choose columns where the same row always has the same value, and the same value is always the same row. A sequence reassigned on every publication makes unchanged rows show as one removed and one added; a retired code handed to something else makes two unrelated things line up as one changed row. Either way the ingest succeeds, so nothing records why. If those are the only candidates, leaving the key unset is the safer answer — without one an edit shows as a row removed and a row added, but two different things are never reported as the same row.
columnSettings.sampleEmpty: This content has no data rows — the columns are all there is.
